question: On 26 August, the US designated the 25-year-old Italian tech collective Autistici/Inventati as a “specially designated global terrorist”1; as a result, the organisation is now also subject to extraterritorial sanctions. The implication of this appears to be a shutdown2, which would be a severe consequence for a European organisation if the designation is incorrect. In light of the above, could the European Commission answer the following questions: 1.

Does the European Commission agree with the US’s classification of the Italian tech collective Autistici/Inventati as a “global terrorist”, and is it aware of any similar classification from any EU Member State, or does it otherwise consider that this tech collective poses a serious threat to security?

If this is not the case, what measures would the Commission consider taking to prevent US extraterritorial sanctions from effectively forcing a European technology organisation such as Autistici/Inventati to close down?

Does the European Commission know how many European companies and organisations have had their existence threatened, or have been forced to close, as a result of extraterritorial sanctions imposed by countries outside the EU?
